LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are some of your school rules?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
   In simple words: practise until you can identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences
   In simple words: practise until you can use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences.
4. Show that you can: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Fill in gaps in sentences using double imperatives,
2. Practise giving instructions related to the theme using double imperatives such as: shut down your tablets and listen to the teacher. Type this word in your tablet and look up its meaning,
3. Role play giving and receiving of instructions at home using double imperatives,
4. Use double imperatives to make rules for their classroom and display them in charts or posters,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of your school rules?
2. How do you give instructions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
